paragraphs: Venus is a sphere wrapped in cloud, which means almost nothing of the surface is visible and everything depends on the atmosphere: pale yellow bands, a subtle rotation pattern and no polar caps or continents to give it landmarks. That featurelessness is exactly what distinguishes it from every other planet at a glance.
The model is built with clean non-overlapping surfaces so a cloud layer and a surface layer can each take their own material, which is how a planet reads correctly when lit from one side.
At $29 it suits astronomy and space visualisation, education and planetarium content, documentary and news graphics, title sequences and motion graphics, and games. On sale since 2016.

A water polo cap is a fabric cap with rigid ear guards moulded into it and a chin strap, and the ear protection is the whole reason it exists: the game is physical and the ears are vulnerable. The number on the side identifies the player, since a swimming cap is the only thing a spectator can read.
The mesh is light at 7,003 polygons and 6,962 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the ear cups and the strap.

A red version sits on this page at the same $29 - the two colours are how the teams are told apart. Both suit aquatic sports visualisation and broadcast graphics, sporting goods retail renders, character set dressing and games. Built to CheckMate specification, on sale since 2025.

A swimwear brief is a stretch garment with no structure at all: the shape comes entirely from the body underneath and from where the fabric is under tension. Elastic edges gather slightly, the fabric is smooth across the front and the side seams are the only construction lines.
The mesh is light at 11,297 polygons and 11,288 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a garment defined by drape rather than by detail.

At $29 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits swimwear and fashion retail renders, beach and resort visualisation, character set dressing for film, television and games, and e-commerce imagery. Real-world scale is kept, so it fits a standard figure. On sale since 2025.

A vertical mouse turns the hand onto its edge so the forearm does not have to twist, which is the whole ergonomic argument. That single rotation changes every surface: the buttons face sideways, the thumb rest becomes a shelf, and the base is narrow because the hand no longer lies flat.
The mesh is efficient at 20,550 polygons and 10,695 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the sculpted shell and the button divisions.

At $29 and built to StemCell specification, it suits consumer electronics and peripheral advertising, desk and office interior visualisation, ergonomics and workplace health material, e-commerce renders and games. On sale since 2024.

A waste oil drainer is a wheeled tank with a wide funnel on a telescoping column, positioned to catch a sump draining above it. The funnel is oversized because nobody aims a drain plug precisely, and the column raises and lowers so it fits under vehicles at different heights.
The mesh is 14,280 polygons and 14,859 vertices, built entirely from quads with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 6 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the paint, the oil staining and the labelling.
At $29 it suits automotive workshop and service visualisation, garage interiors, equipment marketing and catalogues, film and television set dressing, and games. On sale since 2019.

A hi-vis waistcoat is the simplest possible garment: two panels, open sides, a zip or hook fastening and reflective bands across the chest and around the body. The band placement is regulated rather than chosen, because those positions are what make a human outline readable in headlights.

The mesh is minimal at 3,088 polygons and 3,086 vertices, built entirely from quads with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 6 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the fluorescent fabric and the retroreflective banding.

An orange version sits on this page at the same $29. Both suit construction and industrial visualisation, safety and training material, roadworks and site scenes, character set dressing and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2020.

Baby food packaging is deliberately reassuring: a short wide glass jar with a metal twist lid, a wraparound label that leaves most of the glass visible so the contents can be seen, and a size that matches a single feed. That visibility of the food is the whole marketing argument.
The mesh is light at 13,216 polygons and 6,614 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the lid as a separate body so it can be shown fitted or removed.
At $24 it suits baby care and food packaging visualisation, brand and label mockups, supermarket and pharmacy renders, e-commerce imagery and games. On sale since 2023.

An emoji rendered in three dimensions is a design translation rather than a modelling job. The flat symbol has no depth, no back and no sense of material, so a solid version has to decide all three while keeping the silhouette instantly recognisable from the original glyph.
The mesh is minimal at 1,988 polygons and 2,068 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a stylised object with simple forms and flat colour.
At $24 it suits motion graphics and title work, social media and messaging content, celebration and event advertising, app and interface illustration, and games. On sale since 2022.

This mine is a curved rectangular case on scissor legs with a sight on top and the famous instruction moulded into the front face. The curve is functional, directing the blast in one arc, and the legs let it be aimed - which is why it looks like a small green appliance rather than like ordnance.

The mesh is deliberately minimal at 4,294 polygons and 2,159 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. That is a game asset budget, light enough for a first person view with the detail carried by texture.

At $24 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits games and interactive media, film and television armouries, military training material, documentary work and illustration. Real-world scale is kept. On sale since 2024.

A cordless drill is a pistol grip with a battery in the base and a chuck at the front, and the proportions come from balance: the battery is heavy, so it sits low and forward of the wrist. The torque collar behind the chuck and the trigger with its forward and reverse switch are the other identifying features.
The mesh is efficient at 32,945 polygons and 17,615 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the chuck jaws, the collar and the grip mouldings.
At $24 it suits workshop and DIY visualisation, tool retail and catalogue renders, construction and trades material, home improvement advertising and games. On sale since 2023.

A moon lamp is a printed sphere with a crater texture and a light inside, set on a stand shaped like a cupped hand. The combination is the product: the hand gives scale and a reason for the sphere to hover, and the internal light makes the crater relief read as shadow rather than as print.

The mesh is minimal at 3,356 polygons and 2,503 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is right for a subject where the crater detail comes from texture and the effect from emission.

At $24 and built to StemCell specification, it suits interior and decor visualisation, gift and homeware retail renders, bedroom and lifestyle imagery, e-commerce material and games. On sale since 2024.

A shampoo bottle is designed to be gripped with a wet hand, which is why the body is flattened rather than round and why the sides are slightly waisted. The flip cap opens with a thumb, and the whole thing is meant to stand upside down in a shower so the last of the contents reaches the nozzle.
The mesh is light at 8,982 polygons and 4,497 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the cap as a separate body so it can be shown open or closed.

At $24 and built to StemCell specification, it suits personal care packaging visualisation, brand and label mockups, bathroom interiors, supermarket and e-commerce renders, and games. On sale since 2024.

A single crushed can is a more specific prop than a set: one object, one particular crumple, useful when a scene needs exactly one piece of litter rather than a pile. The printing folds into the creases, which is what makes the deformation read as aluminium rather than as a dented cylinder.

The mesh is minimal at 6,193 polygons and 6,119 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, sensible on a subject whose surface is a repeating wrap, and the StemCell build means it works in a real-time engine.
At $24 it suits recycling and sustainability visualisation, urban and street set dressing, interior clutter, beverage advertising, film and television, and games. On sale since 2026.

A fermenter is a closed vessel with a conical bottom, a cooling jacket around the sides, a manway on the front and a valve at the lowest point so yeast can be drawn off. Every one of those features exists because fermentation produces heat and sediment, and the vessel has to manage both.
It is built in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which lets the polished stainless steel, the jacket welds and the valve fittings each take their own material treatment.

At $24 and built to StemCell specification, it suits brewery and food production visualisation, biotechnology and process industry presentation, plant interiors, equipment marketing and games. On sale since 2025.
